faq.a: Khamisi is associated with the Arabic form خَامِس, whose core sense is khamisi; born on thursday; fifth (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Khamisi?
faq.a: Khamisi is associated with Arabic. Khamisi is the Swahili form of Arabic خَامِس (Khāmis, 'fifth'), used for a child born on Thursday.
Yes — the underlying form خَامِس is Arabic.
Khamisi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Khamisi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Khāmis is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Khamisi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Khamisi is rendered خامس and carries the sense خامس، پانچواں.

faq.q: What does Khamisi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khamisi is rendered خامس and carries the sense خامس، پنجم.
A romanized syllable approximation is kha-mi-si. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khamisi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khamisi, khamisi. Script forms are خامس, خَامِس, ख़ामिस.

faq.q: Is Khamisi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
